key_insight: BSPDN already forces a bonded carrier onto the signal side; making it DRAM adds ~45 GB at ~0.3 pJ/bit interface, with no TSVs, PHYs, interposer or extra footprint.
killer_doubt: BSPDN puts the heat sink on the carrier side, so DRAM sits in the ~1 W/mm2 path at ~95-105 C (2-4x refresh); one bond short scraps a ~$30k logic wafer.
decisive_experiment: D2W hybrid-bond commercial DRAM test dies face-down onto a heater-and-sensor logic die at 2-6 um pitch with bank-disable sparing (~$300k). Measure bond yield, pJ/bit and retention tails at 85-110 C under 1 W/mm2.
prior_art: Chip Scale Review 2022: memory wafer replaces BSPDN carrier (via search snippet); UniIC SeDRAM (IEDM 2020); Graphcore Bow functional carrier; AP Memory VHM WoW.

key_insight: Poising a regenerative amplifier near instability is the right instinct, but the cross-coupled latch already is a saddle-node regenerator; offset cancellation, not bifurcation type, sets sensitivity.
killer_doubt: DRAM reads a DC step; Hopf gain favours periodic tones. A 1 fF cell on 35 fF gives ~14 mV, comparable to 5-10 mV sigma offset that poise amplifies.
decisive_experiment: Transient-noise SPICE plus Monte Carlo mismatch of a Hopf-biased versus offset-cancelled latch on a 35 fF bitline; compare BER for 1-2 fF cells. Build an MPW only if Hopf gives >2x margin. ~$20k.
prior_art: Offset-cancellation sense amps in production DRAM; charge-transfer presensing (study N-04); Hopf hair-cell amplifier circuits in silicon-cochlea work [training knowledge].

key_insight: Retention failures are almost all charged-to-discharged, so a cell-type-aware low-weight code shrinks the vulnerable population at zero process cost.
killer_doubt: 8-bit-group inversion cuts charged cells only ~27% (50% to 36%); on a steep retention tail that stretches tREF ~10-17%, below the 12.5% capacity cost of 16-to-18-bit coding.
decisive_experiment: Replay real traces through the code on DRAM-Bender using true/anti-cell maps of 20 DDR4/DDR5 dies; measure retention failures versus tREF with and without encoding. Kill below 1.3x tREF at equal failures. ~$40k.
prior_art: Liu et al. ISCA 2013 data-pattern dependence; DDR4/5 data-bus inversion; true/anti-cell characterization (Mutlu group); zero-aware refresh schemes [training knowledge].

key_insight: Clean, file-backed pages have an authoritative copy elsewhere, so detection plus refetch can replace correction for a large share of server memory.
killer_doubt: Already published and partly shipped (HRM, Linux hwpoison). Above ~1e-7 BER nearly every 64 B line refetches from SSD at ~50-100 us; below it, it is ordinary tiering.
decisive_experiment: None beyond R17 I-02525's DRAM-Bender study of clustered versus diffuse faults in reject dies; fold the clean-page policy into the I-01312 CXL controller. ~$0 incremental.
prior_art: Heterogeneous-Reliability Memory (Luo et al., DSN 2014); Linux hwpoison clean-page drop; in-study R17 I-02525 and R28 I-10427 (both DROP).

key_insight: Liquid-cooled AI racks hold DIMMs near 30-40 C, where retention is several-fold longer, so a cold-certified grade could absorb hot-fail dies and relax refresh.
killer_doubt: Refresh is ~10-20% of power and bandwidth, so 4x less saves ~8-15%. LPDDR already scales tREFI with temperature via MR4; tail activation ~0.3-0.6 eV caps gain.
decisive_experiment: Thermal-chuck retention-tail maps of 100 hot-test-reject and 100 passing DDR5 dies at 30, 55 and 85 C on an FPGA tester, with 4 weeks of VRT tracking. Count dies passing 256 ms at 35 C. ~$100k.
prior_art: LPDDR4/5 MR4 temperature-based refresh multipliers; DDR 2x refresh above 85 C; Liu ISCA 2013; in-study R19 I-11539 and I-11080 (DROP) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Data-parallel replicas are a free majority vote: periodic cross-replica weight hashes detect and repair HBM or compute corruption in replicated weights.
killer_doubt: Already practiced for SDC detection. FSDP/ZeRO shard weights, so true replicas are few; HBM refresh is per-device, not per-region, so no weak-die or relaxed-refresh saving follows.
decisive_experiment: On a 64-GPU HSDP job, measure the replicated-weight share of HBM, then inject bit errors at 1e-9 to 1e-6 into one replica between hash checks and quantify loss divergence. ~$30k compute.
prior_art: Laguna M.1 report hashes weights across DP replicas; shadow-replica SDC detection (arXiv 2502.12340); AEGIS (OSDI'26) (via search snippet).

key_insight: Decorrelating vendor- and lot-systematic failure modes across a codeword is the right instinct for qualifying second-source or new U.S. dies.
killer_doubt: A 10-chip DDR5 codeword from 3-4 vendors still puts 3-4 same-design chips under identical commands; one vendor's hammer weakness exceeds chipkill's 1-symbol correction. Mixed timings run slowest.
decisive_experiment: Folded into in-study I-04094: build mixed-vendor DDR5 RDIMMs, run TRRespass/U-TRR on an FPGA tester, and count codewords with more than one failing chip versus single-vendor modules. ~$150k.
prior_art: Chipkill (IBM 1997); vendor-correlated field failures (Facebook 2015; Sridharan 2015); TRRespass/U-TRR; in-study I-04094, same mechanism (DROP).

key_insight: Wafer-test fail maps are free data; pairing dies with non-overlapping weak rows lets a buffer or base die borrow spare rows across dies.
killer_doubt: Mature DRAM loses only a few % of dies after on-die redundancy; mirroring halves capacity, and spare sharing needs a remap layer (base die, CXL controller). Gain ~1-3 yield points.
decisive_experiment: Mine wafer-sort fail-bit maps from a partner fab, or 500 reject dies on DRAM-Bender; simulate pairing with a 1k-entry cross-die remap table and count rescued dies versus PPR alone. ~$60k.
prior_art: Redundancy sharing across stacked dies (Jiang et al., ICCAD 2010); wafer matching for W2W yield (Reda et al., 2009); DDR5 PPR [training knowledge].

key_insight: Retired DDR4/DDR5 is wafer-free capacity; in-system retention and hammer profiling with weak-row maps in SPD makes it a trusted CXL tier.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of canonical R16 I-00224 (HOLD). Microsoft GreenSKU and Marvell Structera X already run DDR4 behind CXL; supply caps at ~5-7 EB/yr of retirements.
decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-00224 pilot: retest and retention-profile 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs at 85 C, run a CXL DDR4 expander in a tier-2 cloud, and report yield and landed $/GB. ~$300k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4-reuse controller; ITRenew/Iron Mountain resale; REAPER retention profiling.

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-00845, framed as an industrial line: profile, grade and resell retired DIMMs into tiers behind chipkill and elastic refresh.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00845 and R16 I-00224. Secondary DDR4 prices track the shortage, and a CXL card plus controller adds ~$0.3-0.8/GB, squeezing the margin.
decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-00224 pilot, plus Q4-2026 bid sheets from three ITAD brokers for 64 GB DDR4 RDIMMs to fix the input cost. ~$10k incremental.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; ITRenew/Iron Mountain recertified hyperscale hardware.

key_insight: A signed per-die error map lets a CXL controller retire rows and set per-bank refresh, turning JEDEC rejects into a trusted product rather than grey-market parts.
killer_doubt: Downbins already sell (Micron SpecTek, eTT/UTT). Truly scrapped dies are a few % after redundancy, and host memory controllers cannot load per-die maps; only custom CXL controllers can.
decisive_experiment: Folded into in-study I-05038: map faults in ~500 UTT/downgraded DDR4/DDR5 parts over temperature and time on an FPGA tester; compute map-recoverable good bits per die and broker price spread. ~$120k.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek downgraded parts; ArchShield (ISCA 2013); in-study I-01312 (ADVANCE), I-05038 and I-08260 (HOLD) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Every corrected error is a free, localized sensor: CE events plus the physical adjacency map and DDR5 directed refresh give a firmware-only second line of hammer defense.
killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die ECC hides single-bit flips, so the host's first CE is often already multi-bit; unread victim rows stay invisible until a ~24 h scrub. PRAC handles hammer in-DRAM.
decisive_experiment: On DRAM-Bender, run U-TRR hammer patterns against DDR5 dies with a host-side CE-triggered neighbor-refresh model; measure the share of campaigns caught before an uncorrectable error. ~$50k.
prior_art: JEDEC DDR5 DRFM and PRAC; Linux RAS CE-threshold page offlining; CE-pattern UE prediction in fleet studies; ECCploit (S&P 2019) [training knowledge].
